metadata.title: Recommendations to Reduce the Risk of Transmission of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) by Human Cells, Tissues, and Cellular and Tissue-Based Products (HCT/Ps): Draft Guidance for Industry
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.

candidates.statement: Unless an exception identified in 21 CFR 1271.90(a) applies, you must review relevant 441 medical records for clinical evidence of relevant communicable disease agents and 442 diseases (21 CFR 1271.75). In accordance with 21 CFR 1271.75(d), you must determine 443 to be ineligible any potential donor who exhibits clinical evidence of HIV (Refs. 2-3, 6-7, 444 10-12, 23-24). Examples of clinical evidence of HIV may include: 445
candidates.context: B. Screening a Donor for Clinical Evidence of HIV Infection 439 • A prior positive or reactive screening test for HIV; 447 • Unexplained weight loss; 448 • Unexplained night sweats; 449 • Unexplained generalized rash; 450 • Blue or purple spots on or under the skin or mucous membranes typical of 451 Kaposi’s sarcoma; 452 • Generalized lymphadenopathy (swollen lymph nodes) for longer than one month; 453 • Unexplained temperature of >100.5°F (38.06°C) for more than 10 days; 454 • Unexplained persistent cough or shortness of breath; 455 • Opportunistic infections; 456 • Unexplained persistent diarrhea; and/or 457 • Unexplained persistent white spots or unusual blemishes in the mouth. 458

candidates.statement: 3. An FDA-licensed HIV antigen/HIV 1/O/2 antibody combination assay can 521 be used for the simultaneous qualitative detection of HIV p24 antigen and 522 antibodies to HIV-1 (including group O) and HIV-2. Such a licensed 523 donor screening test should be used in combination with an HIV-1 NAT to 524 adequately and appropriately test an HCT/P donor for HIV-1 and HIV-2. 525
candidates.context: 2. For HIV-2: An FDA-licensed donor screening test either for anti-HIV-2 517 or a combination test for anti-HIV-1 (including group O) and anti-HIV-2 518 (Ref. 167). 519 Any HCT/P donor whose specimen tests negative (or non-reactive) for all assays (i.e., 527 anti-HIV-1 (including group O), anti-HIV-2, or a combination test for those disease 528 agents; and HIV-1 NAT) is considered to be negative (or non-reactive) when making a 529 donor eligibility determination. Note that a negative (or non-reactive) test does not 530 necessarily mean that a donor is eligible; donor screening also applies as described above. 531
